newsitem.title: POLAND: Exporters' orders give Polish zloty brief boost.
newsitem.headline: Exporters' orders give Polish zloty brief boost.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased back to 1.00/0.90 percent above the parity rate from highs of 1.27/1.17 percent in early trade as banks closed positions shortened on Tuesday and took profits after the unit's rise, dealers said.
They said the zloty's upward stab was caused by several exporters' currency sell orders totalling more than $50 million which sparked a speculative currency seling trend on the market.
"The sudden zloty surge was a result of several coinciding large exporters' orders which started a trend and pulled the whole market with it," said Tomasz Wolosz of BRE SA.
"As soon as the market went up to around 1.3 percent from parity, banks started closing positions and taking profits," he said.
At 0910 the zloty was at 3.2845/65 against the dollar and 1.8805/25 against the mark.
